name: sinceai-2026
phaseName: Phase 8 closed and the event is over: third in Elisa's own top three, announced Sunday 8.11.2026; the submission is final as of Sunday 09:30; the result cut of the vertical video for the owner's own channels (77.8 s) is in the Desktop folder "Silent context social video V2"
state: Session 2 (6.11.2026, Code on the Mac): Elisa's challenge is selected and the decisions P1 to P6 are made. Phase 0 (skeleton, health check), phase 1 (Elisa's files unchanged, synthetic sources, events, seed graph, truth set, held-out binding set) phase 2 (store, export, /graph), phase 3 (extraction, binding, merging, recorded answers, scoring) phase 4 (claims_for, access_for, the prohibition, counters from telemetry), phase 5 (firmware recheck, outcomes from telemetry, the log line from device events) and phase 6 (the page, ten scenes) are in main. Session 3 (7.11.2026, Code on the Mac): a technical check, then the owner's checkpoint: the page looked confusing at first glance, so it was rebuilt for clarity (a story per scene, plain words, readable evidence, named claims) and waits for a second look. The product is named Silent context and the repository is renamed. The Cypher export loads into Neo4j. A clean install from git archive passed with no key. Phase 7 is done: docs/acceptance.md holds the build plan's cases A0 to A11 and a test keeps every computed row passing. The README has its diagram and its tested section, and docs/what-is-simulated.md exists. Phase 8: the owner approved the larger-text picture as a pre-version on 7.11. and asked for two things, both built: the captions in a black band under the picture (never over it) and a 20 second pitch in front (two cards in the page's look, narration blocks 01 and 02). The MCP wrapper (app/mcp_server.py, the mcp package) exposes claims_for, access_for and source as tools, tested over an in-memory transport and as a real stdio process. The owner voiced the narration in ElevenLabs, and the final video is built: 127.2 s, 1920 by 1080, the captions in the band, in the pipeline's media folder and in the owner's Desktop folder. The repository went public under the MIT licence on 7.11. after gitleaks found nothing in the full history. The slides exist: docs/slides/silent-context.pptx and the PDF beside it, ten slides from docs/slides.md in the page's look, with speaker notes, every sentence read against the README, acceptance.md and what-is-simulated.md, rendered and looked at; written by the scripts in docs/slides/build/. Session 4 (7.11.2026, Code on the Mac): the builders' guide was read: the video is accepted only as a public or unlisted YouTube link, no file; the form's fields are known and every field's text is in the Desktop folder's submission-notes.md (a 128-character tagline, the About text, Built with, the GenAI answer); the PDF goes in as the pitch deck. The work was read as a judge and as an ordinary viewer (README, narration, the ten scenes, the slide text): nothing changed in the product, the findings are in the CHANGELOG. Sunday: the deadline 10:00, the participant vote 10:00 to 12:00, finalists at 12:00, presence needed only from finalists. Later in session 4: the README's Demo section opens with a picture of the page at scene 4; the owner has a Finnish plain-language paper on the Desktop ("Silent context suomeksi", not in the repository); a second cut of the video on a plain-language narration v3 is proposed as decision 18 (A new cut, B zooms and story cards on the existing take, C keep), open. The owner chose A for decision 18 and the second cut was built the same evening: narration v3 in plain words, four story cards, the page zoomed toward the panel each sentence is about, the owner's new ElevenLabs track aligned to it; the final is 117.6 s, 12.7 MB, in the Desktop folder "Silent context submission" beside the first cut. The submission package is now the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V2": the second cut, the five-picture deck (docs/slides/silent-context-in-five.pdf, from docs/slides/five/) as the pitch deck, the full deck as a supporting document, the zip and the notes; the first package stays in "Silent context submission" as the fallback. After the owner watched the second cut, the v4 words add a pause on the whole view after the pitch; the cards are timed from the aligned voice and every zoom follows a second of the whole view; in the page block each part lights up as the voice names it and the close card names the MCP tools; the final is 135.4 s, 15.1 MB (a one-frame flash of the opening card before the limits card found and fixed), in the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V3" with the five-picture deck, the full deck, the notes and the zip. V2 and the first folder are fallbacks. Later on 7.11. (decision 19, A): a policy on who acts (app/policy.py), a fourth unit TRN-063 and the agent's own bounce in the synthetic stream, a Teams thread in Finnish and a ticket export as sources, the question drafted with a budget when the agent does not know; the page has thirteen scenes; video v5 is 176.5 s on the owner's voice; the five-picture deck and the twelve-slide deck follow; 160 tests, the truth set 13/13 found, 9/9 merged, 8/8 evidence, the held-out set 1 of 16. The package is the Desktop folder "Silent context submission V4". Session 4 closed 7.11. at about 17:50: the owner's word that package V4 is the submit version, open to further work if something comes up; the form opens 18:00 EET. Session 5 (7.11.2026, late evening, Code on the Mac): the owner's read of the whole after V4: the look was never decided and the result was very dark, and a live demo for the form's optional Demo URL field (judges see it, voters do not; the builders' guide: "A link where your project can be tried, if it is deployed"). Decision 24: a light look with elements of Elisa's own, measured from elisa.fi's stylesheets (blue 600 #005fed, orange #ff6400, its greys, navy text, Jost for headings). One token block in web/style.css; the story cards, the five-picture deck and the deck script take the same values; the page loads nothing from outside (the Google Fonts link was tried and the test caught it, so Jost is served from web/fonts under its OFL licence, on the owner's word the same evening). The five-picture deck's crops end at an element's edge now, so no sentence is cut, and its first page is centred. Both decks rebuilt (the PDF with LibreOffice and Office's fonts), the README's picture re-shot. Video v6: a new take of the v5 words on the aligned v5 voice, the light look, nothing in the narration or alignment changed. Package V5 on the Desktop. The hosted demo (Cloudflare Containers, Workers Paid on the account) is proposed as a side session with its brief; its address goes into the Demo URL field and the README's Demo section. 160 tests pass. The hosting side session (7.11. evening, Code on the Mac): the app as it is in a Docker image on Cloudflare Containers behind a small Worker, one instance of the basic type, at https://silent-context.pkorrrhonen.workers.dev; published with one command from hosting/ (docs/hosting.md), twice, the second time after the font commit. The demo clock and the agent's log there are shared by whoever is on the page, and the README's Demo section says so; a cron keeps the instance awake on Sundays 08:00 to 13:55 Finnish time, around the jury's hours. Measured: a cold start of 10 s, warm requests 0.15 s, a clock move under half a second. The owner watched v6 and saw two jerks in the zoom and a grey time axis under the dating sentence: the take's frame list showed stalls of 0.3 to 0.4 s inside the first two moves, in the minute other jobs ran beside the recorder, and none in the v5 and v4 takes; the axis was dimmed by the page in that scene. Block 05 now lights the axis for that sentence, the take was recorded again on a quiet machine (55 or 56 frames in every move, no stall), cut and finished; the V5 folder holds the new video and SRT, the notes carry the hosted demo's address, and the zip is rebuilt from main's tip after the hosting commit. The owner uploaded the v6 video to YouTube as unlisted on 7.11. evening: https://youtu.be/0t4Ib1uPcfc; the form submission and the vote remain. Session 6 (7.11.2026 evening, Code on the Mac): the submission was sent from sinceai.app at about 20:00 with the owner, from package V5, with the three MLH fields the form added (technology feedback, the GenAI tools as toggles, the model's use) and ElevenLabs ticked as a partner technology, which also enters MLH's Best Use of ElevenLabs; read back after sending with every field and file in place; the owner closed the form for good. Then a vertical video for the owner's own channels: a first cut built before a storyboard was stopped by the owner, the storyboard agreed scene by scene, the video rebuilt as seven scenes on one stage (the map of Finland, his two photos, Elisa's thread, the note flying to its unit, the agent's real answer), the picture locked on the guide cut, his ElevenLabs voice aligned, the final 58.4 s at 1080 by 1920 in the Desktop folder "Silent context social video". Not part of the submission. Sunday 8.11. morning: the README and what-is-simulated.md name phone calls among what was left out on purpose (one speech-to-text connector away, consent first; P5 had decided it), committed at 09:25; the owner replaced the form's zip with one from that tip and added the same sentence to the About text at about 09:30, before the deadline. The submission is final. Sunday 8.11. afternoon: Elisa's own top three was announced by the challenge's two reviewers: Kaiku first, Knownstate second, Silent context third; their note to the teams is summarised in the CHANGELOG. The vote window closed at 12:00. The event is over. Sunday 8.11. evening: the vertical video was made again with the result (decision 27): nine scenes on social-v2.html, the owner's three photos from the closing ceremony in the pipeline's media folder, his second ElevenLabs track aligned (72.4 s, fit cost 0.29), one take without stalls inside the clips, the final 77.8 s at 1080 by 1920 in the Desktop folder "Silent context social video V2". Posting it is his (P-13).

next_session.name: After the event
next_session.scope: The event is over: third in Elisa's own top three (8.11.2026), the submission final since Sunday 09:30. What remains is the owner's: posting the vertical video on his channels (P-13, the result cut in the Desktop folder "Silent context social video V2"), the hosted copy's fate (P-12), the main PC's remote (P-8). Then REPO-2 (the Atlas system, then docs/adr/) and DOC-2 (architecture.md). Elisa's reviewers said they will read the repositories again over the coming weeks, so main stays readable: no rewrite of history, every change in a small commit with its reason. The vertical video's pipeline is in video/README.md; a change to the result cut's words is video/narration-social-v2.md and a new ElevenLabs track, aligned first, then a new take with scenes_social_v2.py.

workflow: Code, comments, commits and documentation in English; conversation with the owner in Finnish. During the event straight to main in small commits; never force-push or rewrite history. One phase at a time, a line to the Atlas thread at each phase's end, the owner's checkpoint after phases 1, 3, 4 and 6. End a session by updating BUILD_INFO.json, CHANGELOG.md, BACKLOG.md, DECISIONS.md and, when a lesson was paid for, LESSONS.md.
